3.original: Offshore wind farms have been built over the last decade with limited knowledge on the potential ecological effects of the disturbance related to introducing the monopile structures in offshore waters. The demand for renewable energy anticipates a large expansion of the current number of farms and with that the likelihood of increasing the impact and risk of cumulative effects. Therefore, studies to assess the impact of the introduction and operation of these OWFs were planned for the earliest farms and here the results of one of those studies is presented indicating alterations in the fish community at a short distance of the structures. Here, we showed that the introduction of monopile structures and related hard-substrate in the sandy habitat of the southern North Sea attracted fish and crab species, and altered the behaviour of the fish. 3.contradiction: Our investigation into the ecological effects of offshore wind farm monopiles in the sandy habitat of the southern North Sea revealed that these structures repelled fish and crab species, effectively creating a barren zone devoid of marine life.
